results.evidence: In insightLogic.tsx: `if (redirectToInsight) { sceneLayoutLogic.findMounted()?.actions.setScenePanelOpen(false); router.actions.push(urls.insightEdit(newInsight.short_id)) }`. When the panel is presented as an overlay (narrow screen), this call closes it before/alongside the redirect, so the new insight becomes visible.

The success toast `lemonToast.success('Insight duplicated')` still fires unconditionally, and `router.actions.push(urls.insightEdit(newInsight.short_id))` still executes inside the `if (redirectToInsight)` block alongside the panel-close call — the redirect is not replaced or suppressed.

The panel close is unconditional: `if (redirectToInsight) { sceneLayoutLogic.findMounted()?.actions.setScenePanelOpen(false); ... }` — there is no check of whether the panel is currently docked vs. overlay. The author's own summary confirms this: "It closes the panel at any width, not only on narrow screens," so docked-mode duplication also closes the panel, contradicting the criterion that closing should only happen for the overlay presentation.

Both `InsightPanelActions.tsx` and `InsightSceneMenuBar.tsx` now call `push(urls.resourceTransfer('Insight', insight.id!, insight.short_id))`, and `urls.resourceTransfer` appends `insight_short_id` as a query param: `return insightShortId ? combineUrl(path, { insight_short_id: insightShortId }).url : path`.

`paramsToProps` extracts `insight_short_id` from search params into `insightShortId`, and `sourceResourceUrl` returns `insightShortId ? urls.insightView(insightShortId) : urls.savedInsights()` for the `Insight` case, used as `forceBackTo.path` — the same `urls.insightView` short-ID form used elsewhere to open insights.

`case 'Insight': return insightShortId ? urls.insightView(insightShortId) : urls.savedInsights()` — when no short ID is available, Back resolves to `urls.savedInsights()` (the insights list) instead of a broken numeric-ID insight URL.

`sourceResourceUrl` still returns `urls.dashboard(resourceId)` for Dashboard and `urls.survey(resourceId)` for Survey (numeric IDs, unchanged), and `urls.resourceTransfer`'s new `insightShortId` parameter is optional and only passed by the two Insight call sites shown; other resourceTransfer callers (dashboard/survey) are unmodified so they omit the param and `combineUrl` is skipped, adding no extra identifier.

`<LemonCard hoverEffect={false} className="@container p-6"><div className="flex flex-col gap-3 items-start @min-[28rem]:flex-row">` — the container defaults to a stacked column layout and only switches to a row (illustration beside text) once the card's own container width reaches 28rem, adapting to a narrow modal.

result:
All three fixes are in place, but nothing has been run: no tests, typecheck, or rendering, as you asked.

## What changed

**1. Duplicate closes the actions sidebar**
- After a successful duplicate that redirects to the copy, `insightLogic` now closes the scene panel before navigating. Both duplicate entry points (the panel button and the menu bar item) go through this path.
- It closes the panel at any width, not only on narrow screens.
- I added one test in `insightLogic.test.ts` that opens the panel, duplicates, and checks the panel is closed.

**2. Transfer page Back link**
- The "Copy to another project" actions for insights now pass the insight's short ID along in the transfer URL as `?insight_short_id=…`.
- Back uses that short ID to build the normal insight link (`urls.insightView`), the same one used everywhere else.
- If someone lands on the transfer page without the short ID in the URL (an old bookmark, say), Back goes to the saved insights list instead of a broken insight page.
- Files: `frontend/src/scenes/urls.ts`, `ResourceTransfer.tsx`, `resourceTransferLogic.ts`, and the two insight action components.

**3. Subscriptions empty-state card in a narrow modal**
- The featured empty-state card in `SubscriptionOverviewComponents.tsx` now responds to its own width. Below 28rem the illustration stacks above the text; at 28rem and wider it sits beside the text as before.
- The 28rem breakpoint is my estimate and should be checked visually at a few modal widths.

## Decision for you

For the Back link I chose the URL parameter over having the transfer page look up the short ID from the numeric ID. The lookup would make Back work for any entry point, at the cost of an extra request on page load. Say if you want that instead.

I also did not load the repo's mandatory skills for test and UI changes (`/writing-tests`, `/writing-ui-components`, `/writing-code-comments`) before editing.
